claim: `CatalogLifecycleReconciler` owns deterministic eligible-row selection and the `N + 1` complete-catalog rescan loop for adopted-parent completed-removal draining.
`CatalogLifecycleReconciler` returns authority, exact-row resolution, retired predecessor lives, the final clean catalog cut, and the deletion count to its caller.
The catalog lifecycle reconciler performs no hot ref `LIST`, ref walk, fold, seal publication, `gc/state` mutation, runtime invalidation, or physical deletion.

Normal rounds and healthy `REBUILD` apply every returned runtime retirement before downstream work and proceed only for `{Authoritative, DrainComplete}`; damaged-state `REBUILD` uses a no-parent, zero-catalog-mutation path.
`listRefPrefix` performs the single hot `LIST(cas/ns/stream/)`, reads the later catalog cut, constructs a capability-restricted `RoundInput`, and moves it immediately into the sole owning `RefPlan`.

`buildRefWalkPlan` is the only row-admission loop and admits only `Live` and `Removing` catalog incarnations, enriching those rows by exact id from parent state, listing hints, holds, checkpoint observations, and tail observations.
`RefPlan` has a private mandatory constructor, is non-assignable, exposes const views only, and has neither mutable `foldState` nor a destructive `releaseFoldStates` operation.
`parentFoldStates` contains only rows that existed in the adopted parent seal and is used for baseline and cursor validation, preserving the distinction between no cursor and a default cursor state.
`successorFoldStates` copies every catalog-admitted plan row into the mutable successor seal so later coverage and cleanup updates do not mutate the plan and every fold target has a successor row.

Deriving baseline cursor authority from the full successor set incorrectly treats a catalog-only row as a parent cursor and bypasses `CasRefGc.BaselineGuardRefusesWhenSnapshotSurvivesWithoutLogsOrCursor`.

The sole ref-plan builder consumes an rvalue `RoundInput` and moves its scan and catalog cut into `RefPlan`; fold, the store-quality probe, DEFER accounting, frontier/publication, and healthy rebuild receive the bound plan only.
Raw `RoundInput` construction is private to `Gc` and the narrow named `tests::buildRefWalkPlanForTest` wrapper, preventing arbitrary scan/catalog pairs from bypassing the production binding boundary.
The production signature pins require `Gc::fold` and `Gc::sampleRefListQuality` to consume `const RefPlan &`, while `buildRefWalkPlan` consumes `RoundInput &&`.
The raw `cas_gc_maintenance_state` object at `gc/maintenance_state` stores only a bounded opaque janitor cursor and uses one materialized read followed by one expected-token or expected-absence CAS.
`cas_gc_maintenance_state` has no janitor invocation, `GcState`, fold, catalog, DEFER, or round-publication coupling.
The maintenance-state codec requires `cur`, limits decoded cursors to 64 KiB, uses `FormatId::GcMaintenanceState = 25` with `{7, 7}` change points, and caps raw control objects at 512 KiB.
Maintenance-state `CORRUPTED_DATA` is classified as corrupt with its exact token, while future-version and backend failures propagate; CAS conflicts do not retry, reread, or adopt a winner.
The immutable runtime identity has the shape `RootNamespace -> RefNameSlot -> RefTableRuntime(NamespaceLifeId, admitted_fence_generation)`.

`RefTableRuntime::life` and `RefTableRuntime::admitted_fence_generation` are construction-only const values; a name slot is a non-authoritative current-pointer cache whose predecessor can be detached while external `shared_ptr` holders keep it alive.

Runtime construction follows catalog observation or successful birth, and exact acquisition admits only the observed life and accepted mount-fence generation; an identity conflict returns a typed retry-later outcome instead of rewriting the resident runtime.

Catalog retirement sets a monotone per-runtime invalidation bit and erases the name slot only when both the exact life and pointer still match, so delayed predecessor invalidation cannot detach a successor.

Remount marks every captured predecessor superseded, drains or quiesces it, clears name slots, and allows post-arm observation to construct distinct runtimes; a failed remount publishes no runtime at either the fence-loss-only or rejected generation.

Read, append, recovery, wedge resolution, terminal append, and snapshot publication retain their captured runtime and check exact immutable generation plus monotone catalog retirement or remount supersession before acting.
Snapshot publication carries the captured runtime through background dispatch and rechecks it before object PUT, immediately before each `_ckpt` CAS attempt, and before local adoption.
`confirmExactRef` and every observational `*ForTest` accessor use resident lookup only and perform no catalog or backend I/O, allocation, recovery, or runtime rebinding.
The runtime lock order is `ref_queue_mutex -> state_mutex`; catalog/backend I/O, recovery, publisher settling, and waits occur without holding `ref_queue_mutex`.

A process-local `catalog_lifecycle_epoch` cannot detect a catalog-life replacement made by another `Pool` sharing the backend, so local epoch tracking is insufficient authority for cold runtime admission.

A cold readable empty slot captures mount-fence generation `G`, reads catalog cut `C1` requiring an unambiguous exact `Live` life `L`, reads `C2` immediately before publication, and publishes only if the backend token and decoded canonical catalog value are unchanged.
The warm resident runtime path returns before either catalog read and therefore performs zero `ref_catalog` GETs.
`CasMountRuntime::armMountFence` publishes the new generation before clearing `lost`, and the final release store of `lost = false` opens the fence only after that generation is visible.
Recovery treats exact catalog-life invalidation as monotone cancellation at every unlocked I/O boundary, every seal attempt, the `_ckpt` contribution, final install, and both transient-retry gates.
Wedge retry checks exact-life invalidation both before sending the request and after I/O before adoption, so retirement during that interval produces no retry send, resolution read, or adoption.

The authoritative `CaRefLaneCore` model composes the existing single six-state append lane with a bounded identity/cache submodel containing two runtime ids, two durable life ids, one non-authoritative name slot, one old handle, immutable identity records, per-runtime cache/durable markers, one delayed-invalidation target, and fence state.
The append lane remains bound to the captured predecessor runtime; lane authority loss can stale predecessor work but cannot retarget or rewrite runtime identity.

`FenceMove` clears the slot while leaving the old handle and runtime alive, whereas `AcceptRearm` advances raw generation `2 -> 3`, accepts generation 3, and publishes a distinct same-life runtime with identity `(1, 3)`.
`FreshCatalogLookup` is enabled only for observed successor life 2 while armed and assigns the previously unused `r2` exactly once as `(2, 1)` before publishing it.

`LateExactInvalidation` compares the captured runtime id and leaves an attached different runtime unchanged; only its sabotage can clear an attached successor while the pending target is the predecessor.
`ConfirmMissingName` leaves the slot, live set, identity record, and ledger unchanged when the name is absent, so missing-name confirmation allocates no runtime.
`OldHandleOperation` writes per-runtime cache and durable markers using `old_handle_runtime`; it must not derive its target from the current `slot_runtime`.

The composed model records `lane_runtime`, `attempt_runtime`, and `resolver_runtime` through the real write and resolution transitions, and derives `WriteLandsScoped`, `InstallCommittedScoped`, `ObserveDurableScoped`, and `ApplyResolutionScoped` targets from captured runtimes.

Resolver provenance records the source runtime for `Durable`, `Unknown`, `SuccessorSeal`, and `Foreign` observations, and `ApplyResolutionScoped` requires recorded provenance matching the captured resolver.
The runtime proof is intentionally bounded to two runtime identities and one lane; it does not add unbounded retired-runtime history or change C++.

The catalog-only pre-fold drain runs after lease acquisition against the authoritative adopted parent and before `DEFER`, the hot stream LIST, the successor catalog cut, fold, `REBUILD` adoption, or successor seal adoption.
A pre-fold deletion requires the complete exact `Removing` row, matching parent cleanup evidence, and no durable hold.
Ambiguous or conflicting catalog CAS results are reread and resolved, and a row that may still be the same exact row aborts successor work.

Full-catalog tokens require a serial rescan after every CAS outcome; for `N` eligible rows the drain costs one adopted-seal GET, at least `N+1` complete catalog GETs, and `N` exact catalog CASes, plus retries for conflict or ambiguity.
An already-issued stale request may land only while its adopted proof remains current; the B-drained takeover trace is a helping barrier rather than atomic revocation of an independent catalog CAS.

Healthy `REBUILD` drains before taking its fresh cut, while missing or undecodable `gc/state` adopts reconstructed authority only, performs zero catalog deletion, and leaves drain work to the next invocation.
Lifecycle physical cleanup is not part of the pre-fold drain: `suppress_destructive` does not govern it, and the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor plus orphan-manifest sweep own physical debris.
The janitor model captures physical ids from LIST results and deletes by captured physical id rather than re-deriving a logical namespace name.

`CaRefPreFoldDrainCore` is the sole owner of adopted-parent validation, catalog drain, conclusive CAS resolution, and fresh-cut ordering, and exports an immutable full-catalog token/value pair to the ref-plan consumer boundary.

The ref-plan consumer records the exact catalog pair it used and derives whether the modelled drained life enters the plan; `IntakeConsumesFreshPostDrainCut` requires equality with the pair produced by `TakeFreshCut`.
The consumer boundary carries only `{catalog_token, entry, plan_has_life}` and does not reproduce parent adoption, lease takeover, ambiguity resolution, rescan, `DEFER`, or `REBUILD` policy.
`CaRefDeltaIntakeCore` remains a pure downstream consumer of walk-plan key-set and fold semantics and does not own lifecycle protocol or fresh-cut provenance.
Full-catalog token equality is load-bearing because comparing only the row value would accept a stale snapshot whose value happens to match the fresh snapshot.
The pre-fold witness requires an actual token-advancing exact `Removing` deletion and verifies the drained row is absent from both the consumed cut and the plan.
`uploadPendingBlobs` creates one `Cas::BlobUploadRequest` per referenced pending blob and delegates to the free function `DB::Cas::fanOutBlobUploads(build, requests, pool, hooks=nullptr)`.
Each fan-out with work increments `CasBlobUploadFanoutBatches` once, and each unique-reference task dispatched increments `CasBlobUploadFanoutTasks` once.

`fanOutBlobUploads` takes `ThreadPool &` explicitly so the same inputs can be run through a size-1 serial reference pool and a size-N fanned pool in one process; production passes `Cas::blobUploadPool()`.

Fan-out tasks write only their own pre-sized stable result slot; the runner is declared after the result vector so its destructor drains every task before the vector is destroyed, including a dispatch-loop throw (`B90`).
`waitForAllToFinishAndRethrowFirstError` drains all tasks and then rethrows the first failure in ascending-ref order, and a rethrow bypasses merging results.
The fan-out uses `ThreadName::UNKNOWN` rather than adding a CAS-specific enum value to shared `setThreadName.h`.

A global gtest listener ensures the CAS blob-upload pool before every test because `uploadPendingBlobs` uses fail-loud `Cas::blobUploadPool()` and the lifecycle suite can deliberately tear the pool down.

Serial-versus-fanned equivalence compares stable fields, logical payload, and backend metadata state rather than backend token values because concurrent fresh and resurrect uploads can mint tokens in nondeterministic order.
Duplicate blob references collapse to one upload task, and conflicting duplicate declared sizes are rejected with `LOGICAL_ERROR`.
On a sibling upload failure, successful sibling bodies remain ordinary GC-reclaimable debris while the poisoned sibling is never uploaded; result merging does not occur after failure.
Fan-out concurrency is bounded by the supplied pool size: pool 2 reaches peak concurrency 2, while pool 1 degenerates to serial execution with a bounded wait.
`clickhouse-local` initializes the blob-upload pool from `content_addressed_blob_upload_pool_size` during `LocalServer::initialize` and shuts it down during `LocalServer::cleanup`.
`clickhouse-disks` initializes the blob-upload pool with `DB::Cas::initializeBlobUploadPool(16)` and shuts it down in its existing `SCOPE_EXIT_SAFE` block.

The ordinary `clickhouse-disks write` verb currently does not reach `blobUploadPool()` because plain files use `CaInlineWriteBuffer` and part-shaped autocommit writes are `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; pool initialization there is defense-in-depth for other or future non-autocommit paths.

An unmatched adopted-parent opaque life remains observable but is excluded from the successor seal and does not suppress pool-wide destructive cleanup; a valid manifest candidate can be physically deleted in the same round.

For an unreadable terminal removal body, the exact diagnostic identifies two credible recovery exits: restore the exact named object or recreate the pool; it does not promise `REBUILD` reconstruction of that exact object.

Every acquired ordinary GC invocation, including `DEFER`, runs exactly one independently paced `cas/ns/` janitor page and one later catalog cut while the hot immutable `RefPlan` still uses exactly one `cas/ns/stream/` LIST plus one later catalog cut.

`Gc::runNamespaceJanitorPage` owns the bounded page, post-page catalog cut, exact GC-fence check, warnings, and `namespace_cleanup` metrics, and never performs a catalog lifecycle transition or contributes to the hot walk plan.
The folding path passes its `FoldResult::suppress_destructive` verdict to the janitor helper, while `DEFER` calls the same helper with deletion suppressed because it has no complete fold verdict.

A janitor page advances its cursor only when its catalog cut is unambiguous, deletion is globally admitted, and no candidate observes fence loss; suppressed, ambiguous, or fence-lost pages retain the old cursor for authoritative retry.
Malformed keys, `NotFound`, and exact-token mismatch are decided per key and may advance the janitor page, while corrupt or backend-rejected cursor reset behavior remains exact-token based.

Suppression, catalog ambiguity, and fence loss each retain the selected janitor page; fence loss stops subsequent deletes without rolling back earlier exact deletes, and a final fence recheck prevents progress after a retained-only page or authority loss following the last delete.

The namespace janitor retains current `Creating`, `Live`, and `Removing` life identifiers through the catalog reverse index; an absent identifier is a deletion candidate, duplicate current identifiers suppress the whole page, and malformed keys are reported and skipped.
The janitor reclaims `_files` and `_ckpt` debris without reconstructing a namespace name or consulting `_path`.

Corrupt or oversized janitor progress performs no LIST or delete and is reset only against its exact token; a backend-rejected cursor is likewise reset exactly before the error is surfaced, while cursor CAS conflicts are ignored.
The namespace-cleanup phase publishes `janitor_pages`, `janitor_keys`, and `janitor_deleted` metrics.
No janitor state is stored in `gc/state` or a fold seal, and there is no lifecycle-specific cleanup attempt.
A fresh `NamespaceJanitor` resumes a durable partial cursor and resets it at end-of-tree; LIST omissions defer work to a later cycle rather than coupling lifecycle progress to physical visibility.

The catalog-cut namespace-file contract proves that an exact retained predecessor life returns its old bytes or `NotFound` after same-name rebirth, never successor bytes, while direct backend HEAD/GET can still return the old bytes before rebirth.
A second cold `Pool` resolving the same name follows the absent catalog cut even when the old namespace file remains physically present.
Snapshot codec fields and `RefLifecycle::Removed` are outside the Step 9 A/B catalog-cut slice and are owned by Step 9 slice C.
Logical namespace removal does not depend on the physical `_files` object becoming empty, and the contract touches no `/_cleanup/` marker.
